title: Dynamic Node Construction on XOR
summary: A deterministic paper-faithful vertical slice exposing Ash's normalized plateau trigger, one-node insertion, and continued backpropagation.
learning_objectives: Calculate the normalized error drop that triggers node insertion.
Observe small-weight insertion without resetting the trained network.
Compare continued ordinary backpropagation with a fixed two-node baseline.
Vary the plateau window and threshold and inspect their effect on growth.
limitations: This is an automated, not-human-reviewed vertical slice, not a reproduction of all experiments in Ash (1989).
XOR is paper-listed, but the deterministic LCG, fixed example order, 250-sweep window, 0.002 trigger threshold, one-insertion cap, and trace rounding are explicit reproduction choices.
The paper reports a 1000-sweep window and 0.05 trigger threshold for most experiments; those settings are exposed as context but shortened here to keep the browser run immediate.
The paper says all new weights are small random values but does not specify a fresh-node-only random sequence; this implementation continues one documented LCG stream.
The fixed-width comparator matches Ash's same-final-topology comparison in shape and training rule, but does not claim statistical equivalence from one deterministic run.
